notes: Account summary: large EU wealth-management firm building unified search + RAG for advisor desktop.
Primary goals: reduce time-to-answer for advisors, add regulatory Q&A, derive intent clusters from transaction notes.
Scale: currently ~120M small documents (snippets + statements) with expected growth to ~500M indexed vectors in 18 months.
Latency targets: p95 end-to-end <150-200ms for search rerank path (recall+rerank), tail <300ms acceptable for heavy rerank.
Throughput: baseline 200 qps for peak; batch background reindexing windows at night. Burst to 1k qps during earnings cycles.
Cost sensitivity: internal target cost-per-query <= $0.004 at 200 qps sustained; cost impacts procurement decision.
Model preferences: embedding dim 1536 (OpenAI-compatible) for initial POC; prefer deployable reranker (light T5 cross-encoder) for privacy.
Architecture preference: hybrid retrieval -> BM25 (Elastic) + ANN recall -> cross-encoder rerank. Also exploring pgvector for transactional data where latency must be single-digit ms.

Connector wishlist: bulk S3-to-vector bulkUpsert; incremental upsert API supporting per-doc metadata and multitenant namespace; support for hybrid BM25 + vector join; ability to expose metadata filters efficiently (AND/OR); metrics for upsert latency and index build time.

Vector DB requirements: HNSW parameter tuning (efConstruction/efSearch), support for quantized indices for cost reduction, warm cache hooks, near-real-time upsert visibility (<5s ideal), and strong export/backup for audit.
Operational: need RBAC & per-namespace KMS integration, audit logs with >12 month retention, SSO + SCIM for user sync.
Quote from CTO: 'We need predictable unit economics. If the numbers don't map for 200 qps, we can't justify managed services.'
Current prototype: internal team built a pgvector PoC with local HNSW; results ok but ingest rate and operational costs are high.
Redwood fit: saw interest in Dedicated for predictable throughput and Private (VPC or on-prem) for EU residency + KMS controls.
Decision makers: Head of Search (Eva Laurent), CTO (R. Mehta), Procurement lead (Simon K.).
Procurement timeline: security sign-off + budget approval expected by May; piloting in April-May.
Key technical question outstanding: how does Redwood routing handle fallback to cheaper model variants under capacity pressure? need SLA on fallback latency/quality.
Other notes: prefer connectors that can hybridize Elastic BM25 + vector store without double-ingest logic on the app side.
